Compare fitted joint models

Source: R/anova.mjoint.R
anova.mjoint.Rd

Compare two or more fitted joint models using their joint log-likelihoods, AIC, and BIC. For nested covariate models, also calculate likelihood-ratio statistics and approximate chi-squared p-values.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mjoint'
anova(object, ..., test = TRUE, nMC = 10000L, tol = 0.1)

Arguments

object

an object inheriting from class mjoint.

...

additional fitted mjoint objects, ordered from the reduced model to the full model when test = TRUE.

test

logical: calculate likelihood-ratio tests between successive models? Default is TRUE. With FALSE, report the stored log-likelihoods, AIC, and BIC without testing or further integration.

nMC

an integer of at least 2 giving the number of Halton integration points per subject used to re-evaluate each likelihood when testing. Default is 10000. The first floor(nMC / 2) points are also used to assess numerical stability.

tol

a positive finite tolerance for the absolute change in the likelihood-ratio statistic between the two integration sizes. Default is 0.1. This is a numerical diagnostic, not a significance threshold or a bound on integration error.

Value

An object of class anova, also inheriting from data.frame, with one row per model. Columns df, logLik, AIC, and BIC describe each model. When testing, L.Ratio, Df, and Pr(>Chisq) describe comparisons with the preceding model, and LR.change is the absolute change in the statistic between the two integration sizes. The integration attribute records the method, integration sizes, tolerance, and likelihoods at the smaller size.

Details

All models must have converged and use the same subjects, longitudinal responses and measurement times, and survival responses. Longitudinal response expressions must also agree, so comparisons between different response transformations are rejected. Models fitted with pfs = FALSE are supported. Older fitted objects that lack the stored fitting matrices must be refitted with the current version of mjoint.

Tests require unchanged random-effects and association structures, and nested longitudinal fixed-effects and survival-covariate design matrices. Each successive model must add at least one identifiable coefficient. Nesting is checked using matrix column spaces, allowing different factor contrasts. The reference distribution is chi-squared, with degrees of freedom equal to the difference in parameter counts. The common baseline hazard has the same event-time support in both models and does not add to this difference. Tests that change the random-effects structure, including tests of zero variance components, are not supported. Non-nested models on the same observations can be compared with test = FALSE.

When testing, the observed joint likelihood is re-evaluated at the fitted coefficients using common deterministic Halton points for the conditional Gaussian random effects. No models are refitted. The table's log-likelihood, AIC, and BIC use these re-evaluated values, so they may differ from the corresponding values stored in the fitted objects. BIC uses the number of subjects. Neither the fitted objects nor R's random-number state is changed.

A warning is issued and the p-value is set to NA if a likelihood-ratio statistic is negative or changes by more than tol when the number of integration points increases. Increase nMC to investigate integration error. A negative statistic can also indicate that a fitted model needs tighter convergence settings or better initial values. Passing this diagnostic does not establish that either model reached the maximum, or guarantee accurate integration or validity of the asymptotic approximation.

A single-model call is not supported; no sequential term deletion or automatic model fitting is performed.

See also

mjoint, logLik.mjoint.

Author

Graeme L. Hickey (graemeleehickey@gmail.com)

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
data(heart.valve)
hvd <- heart.valve[!is.na(heart.valve$log.lvmi), ]
reduced <- mjoint(
  formLongFixed = log.lvmi ~ time,
  formLongRandom = ~ 1 | num,
  formSurv = Surv(fuyrs, status) ~ age,
  data = hvd, timeVar = "time", seed = 123)
full <- update(reduced, formLongFixed = log.lvmi ~ time + sex)
anova(reduced, full)
# Check sensitivity to more integration points
anova(reduced, full, nMC = 20000)
# Descriptive comparison using the stored likelihoods
anova(reduced, full, test = FALSE)
} # }
